answer: A durable anti-sybil defence is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable stake that cannot be copied cheaply. Like a river that only carries real flow, an agent economy should require each identity to lock a small refundable deposit — an opal-grade bond — and earn reputation through sustained, auditable work before it can transact at full volume. A sudden gale of new accounts would then face real cost: each fake identity must fund its own bond and build history, while honest agents keep theirs. Sybils become expensive to spawn at scale, and misbehaviour forfeits the bond.
